claims.statement: The error-genealogy method routes every raw trace error through five deterministic, LLM-free links — E0 granularity (what counts as one error event), E1 symptom (family + signature, description/provenance only, does not decide), E2 mechanism (the agent's actual mistake, the diagnosis), E3 unit (mechanisms grouped by a shared preventing lesson), and E4/E5 triage (candidate / non-memory / out, a decision rather than a taxonomy level).

Symptom (E1) and mechanism (E2) classification are two independent readings of the same error message with independent roles (describe vs. decide) rather than independently-coded pipelines; the mechanism axis adds exactly one local evidence signal the symptom axis never reads (e.g., the rejected code line), and the two axes relate many-to-many in both directions, so a tree cannot represent them — the symptom axis never feeds the triage decision.

The genealogy's edge cardinalities are symptom→mechanism = 1:N (the taxonomy divides: one surface complaint admits multiple causes), mechanism→unit = N:1 (the taxonomy fuses: different causes needing the same fix converge), and unit→decision = N:1 decided at the global unit level, not per (context × unit).

In the trace-law-flow instantiation, the 136 errors sharing the symptom signature 'Could not index' split into three distinct mechanisms via submecanismo() reading the rejected code line — dict_indexado_por_posicao (89), tipo_real_do_retorno (37), and campo_inexistente_no_retorno (10) — and the first two (plus a third mechanism born of a different symptom) converge into the same memory unit (U_contrato_dict, 96 errors) because one lesson prevents both, while campo_inexistente_no_retorno remains a separate unit because no single sentence could cover both causes without becoming a disjunction.

Writing memory at the symptom level instead of the unit level fails in two opposite ways simultaneously: a symptom that splits into multiple mechanisms produces an ambiguous, diluted card (a checklist of possible causes with different fixes, and a non-injective routing key since re-running the mechanism classifier would still be required), while a symptom whose mechanism is shared with another symptom produces a duplicated card (the same lesson written twice, doubling maintenance cost and risking divergence).

A memory unit is only triaged as a candidate after passing three ordered gating questions — (1) is this the agent's own memory to learn from, as opposed to a harness/upstream-LLM failure routed to operational policy instead; (2) does the unit have unique, single-sentence content — residual buckets that fail this go to 'revisar', the taxonomy work-queue, rather than being discarded; (3) does it recur across executions and over time — and the recurrence thresholds (execution count, time window) are calibrated per instantiation rather than being fixed constants of the method, requiring an explicit sensitivity test.

The method's construction order deliberately starts from the raw trace and only afterward tests the resulting taxonomy against the literature, which is restricted to three roles — testing the mapping against external taxonomies, suggesting analyses not yet run, and lending vocabulary — and is never allowed to supply the taxonomy's categories directly, since that would make the result an import rather than a genealogy grounded in the trace.

A prior version of the trace-law-flow memory-candidate table overclaimed that AgentDebug's finding was 'the module that produced the error routes the memory type'; checking the full 32-page PDF (arXiv:2509.25370) found zero occurrences of routing or memory-type language — the paper proposes a 5-module diagnostic taxonomy and an ablation showing root-cause-only correction beats fixing every surface mistake, but the routing claim was the project's own analogy, not a transferred finding, and was corrected in three files the same day.

AgentDebug and TRAIL classify agent errors along genuinely different, complementary axes rather than being redundant or competing: AgentDebug classifies by which cognitive module produced the error and outputs prescriptive correction_guidance, while TRAIL classifies by phenomenon (20 leaf error types) with a per-error impact severity field and a diagnostic output — AgentDebug informs the shape of a memory unit, TRAIL informs coverage measurement and prioritization by cost.

The method declares six explicit limits: only exceptions that raise are counted (silent failures need separate detectors); the symptom axis's family/signature names already carry causal interpretation rather than being neutral surface labels; the method reads what the trace shows, not agent intent; there is no severity-of-consequence axis alongside frequency and cost; cascade deduplication looks only at a short window of consecutive steps; and triage recurrence thresholds are calibrated choices requiring sensitivity testing, not fixed constants.

The classifier's residual is split into two non-overlapping buckets — 'Sintoma não reconhecido' (neither E1 nor E2 recognizes the message: a coverage alarm that asks for a symptom rule first) and 'Causa não identificada' (symptom known, cause unknown: asks only for a cause rule, and includes malformed-code noise until proven recurrent). Each error lands in at most one bucket, bucket size is part of an instantiation's coverage report, and both buckets pass the same recurrence test as candidates but counted per masked error pattern — a recurring pattern yields 'revisar — prioridade', otherwise 'revisar — baixa prioridade'.

The single declared exception to 'the symptom axis never feeds the decision': montar_unidades() consults the classify() family only to separate the two residual buckets (causa_sem_regra + 'Sintoma não reconhecido' family → sintoma_nao_reconhecido) — buckets that never become memory; all 10 base-1 candidates are identical with or without that separation.
